routes.description: Establish that theism offers a better overall explanation by supplying a non-causal ground for contingent reality, a principled ultimate explanatory terminus, and an epistemically coherent account of religious experience and diversity.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if the theistic resources jointly provide material explanatory advantages over naturalistic alternatives while meeting challenges concerning brute necessity, experiential unreliability, divine communication, and religious disagreement.

motionBridge.description: Show that theism's combined treatment of contingent reality and religious experience makes it the better overall explanation relative to naturalism.

centralBridges.description: Require a non-causal and non-necessitating explanation of the contingent total causal history and identify divine free grounding as the relevant resource.
Provide a principled ultimate terminus whose essence entails existence and explain why a theistic candidate has comparative explanatory relevance.
Justify giving context-sensitive evidential weight to religious experience, testimony, and cultivated religious practices.
Account for ambiguity and religious diversity without requiring that divine communication chiefly produce uniform and detailed theology.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Specify grounding as the relation by which divine creative activity could unify and explain created causal reality.
Distinguish degrees of experiential and testimonial reliability while preserving qualified trust amid disagreement.

routes.description: Establish that naturalism can match or exceed theism's explanatory coverage without adding God by offering naturalistic foundations for contingent history and explaining religious phenomena through calibrated cognition, social processes, and nonintentional causes.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if naturalistic accounts cover the principal explanatory domains without a uniquely theistic resource and if the proposed theistic stopping points and experiential expectations do not establish an overall comparative advantage.

motionBridge.description: Show that adding God does not improve the overall explanation once naturalistic alternatives and the comparative costs of theistic explanations are included.

centralBridges.description: Supply a naturalistic structure in which necessary initial reality and indeterministic evolution explain the occurrence of a contingent history.
Require equal scrutiny of naturalistic and theistic ultimate necessities and deny an asymmetry based only on naming a developed divine essence.
Explain why religious experience must be calibrated for ordinary unreliability, cognitive mechanisms, and the relevant comparison class.
Relate ambiguity, unsuccessful visionaries, and enduring religious diversity to the expectations of intentional divine communication and naturalistic causation.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Compare explanatory coverage and simplicity across complete worldviews without double-counting a disputed explanatory deficiency.
Preserve live naturalistic ultimate candidates where present knowledge of cosmic origins does not determine their essential structure.

sections.title: Standards for Comparing Complete Worldviews
sections.rationale: This issue fixes how explanatory coverage, simplicity, uncertainty, and reasonable disagreement bear on the motion, and therefore governs how the more specific causal and experiential disputes contribute to an overall comparison.

sections.title: Grounding and the Explanation of Contingent Causal History
sections.rationale: The debate's principal metaphysical clash concerns whether contingent causal history requires a non-causal, non-necessitating ground or can be explained through necessary natural conditions with indeterministic evolution.

sections.title: Necessary Existence and Explanatory Termination
sections.rationale: This issue determines whether theism supplies a principled ultimate explanatory terminus unavailable to naturalism, or whether divine and natural foundations face symmetrical demands concerning necessity, essence, and bruteness.

sections.title: Epistemic Weight and Naturalistic Calibration of Religious Experience
sections.rationale: Religious experience is a distinct proposed source of comparative support whose force depends on default trust, testimonial and first-person justification, learned practices, cognitive mechanisms, and calibrated unreliability.

sections.title: Divine Communication, Visionaries, and Religious Diversity
sections.rationale: The distribution, ambiguity, and durability of divergent traditions test whether religious phenomena fit intentional divine relationship or nonintentional natural and sociological processes within the competing worldviews.

moves.speaker: Graham Oppy
moves.proposition: Naturalists can construct a comparably explanatory worldview without adding God, regardless of the broad shape of causal reality.
moves.attributionBasis: The moderator explicitly gives Graham Oppy the first opening statement, and the uninterrupted first-person exposition is his.

response.rationale: This constructive move establishes the naturalistic comparative program and therefore has no earlier opposing move to answer.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within constructive moves, it clearly states the overall comparative thesis but only sketches the supporting argument.

precisionFindings.rationale: The comparative claim is recoverable, though the breadth of causal shapes and the standard of comparability remain compressed.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The move claims that a naturalistic construction is available, and its exploratory framing fits that modest force.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The proposed comparative strategy is coherent, but the bridge from causal-shape neutrality to comparable explanation is compressed.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The excerpt states a general program and its origin but supplies little representative support or comparison with theistic rivals.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It directly advances the naturalistic route's motion-level claim of overall explanatory comparability.

representationalCharity.rationale: The move advances its own program without developing a meaningful opposing interpretation for a charity test.

moves.evidenceBasis: Oppy says naturalists can argue for their worldview regardless of the broad shape assigned to causal reality.

moves.speaker: Graham Oppy
moves.proposition: Comparing explanatory coverage and theoretical simplicity requires judgment and can permit reasonable disagreement rather than yielding an algorithmically decisive result.
moves.attributionBasis: The moderator proposes a characterization, after which Oppy qualifies it in a sustained first-person response.

response.rationale: This constructive methodological move explains how worldview comparison involves judgment and allows reasonable disagreement without answering an earlier opposition move.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within constructive moves, it gives a clear methodological qualification that directly structures the later comparison.

precisionFindings.rationale: The claim about judgment, reasonable alternatives, and nonalgorithmic comparison is stated with express qualifications.

calibrationFindings.rationale: Oppy expressly allows reasonable contrary judgment, matching the modest methodological conclusion to the support offered.

charity.alternative: A reasonable evaluator may judge the competing worldview virtues differently.
charity.decisiveQualification: Reasonable disagreement does not imply that arguments identify no genuine comparative considerations.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The distinction between considerations and a uniquely decisive algorithm is consistent and clearly maintained.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The methodological conclusion is plausibly motivated, though no developed account of weighing coverage against simplicity is supplied.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It materially supports the subsidiary burden governing comparative worldview method and reasonable disagreement.

representationalCharity.rationale: The move explicitly recognizes the reasonable alternative judgment rather than treating disagreement as irrational.

moves.evidenceBasis: Oppy explicitly calls the comparison a matter of judgment and concedes that an alternative judgment may be reasonable.

moves.speaker: Kenny Pearce
moves.proposition: Arguments can identify genuine considerations favoring theism or naturalism even when there is no agreed algorithm for uniquely balancing all worldview virtues.
moves.attributionBasis: The moderator directly invites Kenny Pearce to present his case, and Pearce begins with an explicit statement of agreement and disagreement.

components.text: Whether reasonable disagreement leaves arguments able to identify genuine comparative reasons and advantages.

response.rationale: Pearce accepts the absence of an agreed decisive algorithm but directly preserves a role for arguments in identifying reasons favoring either worldview.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: The reply explicitly contacts the methodological inference and gives a clear, bounded qualification rather than merely changing topics.

precisionFindings.rationale: The distinction between uniquely settling the comparison and identifying genuine reasons is stable and explicit.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The limited claim that arguments can call attention to reasons is appropriately matched to the acknowledged disagreement.

charity.alternative: Worldview virtues may permit more than one reasonable overall judgment.
charity.decisiveQualification: That underdetermination does not eliminate local arguments about where particular advantages lie.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The concession and qualification fit together cleanly, and the conclusion follows without treating local reasons as an algorithm.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The conceptual distinction is well defended, though concrete examples of comparative advantages are deferred to later moves.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It directly attacks an overstrong reading of the subsidiary comparative-method burden without itself completing the motion.

representationalCharity.rationale: Pearce expressly accepts the reasonable-disagreement premise and narrows his disagreement to the role of particular reasons.

moves.evidenceBasis: Pearce agrees that disagreement need not make someone wrong while insisting that arguments identify reasons favoring either side.

moves.speaker: Kenny Pearce
moves.proposition: The contingent total causal history requires a non-causal and non-necessitating explanation, for which divine free grounding supplies a resource not identified within science-oriented naturalism.
moves.attributionBasis: Pearce identifies this as his contingency argument and develops it continuously, with only brief clarifying interventions from the moderator.

components.text: Whether naturalism can match theism's explanatory resources across possible structures of causal reality.
Whether a specific explanatory consideration can favor one worldview despite reasonable overall disagreement.

response.rationale: Pearce identifies a specific alleged naturalistic deficit: explaining a contingent total history in a noncausal and nonnecessitating manner, and proposes divine freedom as the contrasting resource.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: The reply directly supplies a proposed comparative disadvantage for naturalism, though it does not exhaust the broad worldview claim.

precisionFindings.rationale: The demanded kind of explanation and the science-oriented scope of the naturalistic criticism are expressly identified.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The science-oriented qualification is explicit, but the claimed absence of a naturalistic explanatory pattern exceeds the support shown.

charity.alternative: Naturalism may contain noncausal or indeterministic explanatory resources not modeled on familiar deterministic science.
charity.decisiveQualification: Pearce limits the challenge to naturalists taking their principal explanatory cues from science.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The inference is intelligible, but the premise that contingency requires a nonnecessitating explanation is asserted more than defended.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The argument identifies a precise explanatory gap, yet the broad negative claim about naturalistic resources lacks representative comparison.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It directly supports the indispensable pro bridge concerning contingent history and divine free grounding.

representationalCharity.rationale: The limitation avoids a universal caricature, although the range of serious naturalistic grounding proposals is not examined.

moves.evidenceBasis: Pearce argues that contingent history needs an explanation that is both noncausal and nonnecessitating and contrasts divine freedom with science-oriented naturalism.

moves.speaker: Kenny Pearce
moves.proposition: Creation is appropriately understood as grounding: God's creative activity is a more fundamental reality that unifies and explains the created causal world.
moves.attributionBasis: After the moderator requests clarification, Pearce defines grounding and applies the concept explicitly to God's creative activity.

response.rationale: This constructive clarification identifies grounding as the intended relation between divine creative activity and created causal reality.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within constructive moves, it clearly specifies the relation needed by the preceding contingency argument, though briefly.

precisionFindings.rationale: Grounding is consistently presented as a more-fundamental relation that explains and unifies created reality.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The proposal is framed as the correct theistic way to understand creation, with support appropriate to a conceptual model.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The application of grounding to creation is internally consistent, with only the grounding-to-explanation bridge left partly implicit.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: Analogies to familiar grounding relations provide some support, but the applicability to divine activity remains compressed.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It strongly supports the subsidiary pro bridge specifying how creative grounding would unify causal reality.

representationalCharity.rationale: The move primarily clarifies its own metaphysical model and does not engage a developed opposing interpretation.

moves.evidenceBasis: Pearce describes God's creative activity as a more fundamental underlying reality explaining and unifying the created world.

moves.speaker: Graham Oppy
moves.proposition: A necessary initial state together with necessary but indeterministic evolution can explain the occurrence of a contingent natural history without an additional non-natural ground.
moves.attributionBasis: The moderator hands the discussion to Graham, who explicitly pushes back and presents the naturalist alternative in the first person.

components.text: Whether contingent history requires an additional noncausal and nonnecessitating ground beyond natural reality.
Whether divine grounding is needed to produce and explain a contingent causal history.

response.rationale: Oppy supplies a direct naturalistic countermodel in which a necessary initial state and necessary indeterministic evolution yield a contingent history without an additional ground.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: The countermodel explicitly contacts the claimed explanatory necessity and states the consequence that no further entity is required.

precisionFindings.rationale: The initial-state, necessary-evolution, and indeterministic-outcome components are recoverable and used consistently.

calibrationFindings.rationale: A countermodel needs to establish availability rather than actuality, and the stated modal force fits that role.

charity.alternative: The occurrence of this particular history may still require a contrastive reason beyond indeterministic laws.
charity.decisiveQualification: Oppy's model explains how contingency can arise naturally, not why this exact outcome rather than another occurs.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The countermodel coherently separates necessary laws from nondetermined outcomes, leaving only the contrastive-explanation issue open.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The modal model is specific and relevant, though its metaphysical possibility and explanatory adequacy are not independently defended.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It directly supports the con route's indispensable natural-history bridge with a concrete explanatory structure.

representationalCharity.rationale: The reply fairly targets the necessity claim but does not fully resolve the stronger contrastive explanatory demand.

moves.evidenceBasis: Oppy proposes a necessary initial state with necessary but indeterministic evolution, yielding contingent history without anything further.

moves.speaker: Graham Oppy
moves.proposition: Postulating a necessary God does not remove explanatory bruteness unless divine necessity can be explained using resources unavailable to the naturalist.
moves.attributionBasis: Oppy begins a direct hypothetical challenge to the necessary-God proposal and contrasts it with his preceding naturalistic account.

components.text: Whether appealing to a necessary God explains the ultimate starting point rather than relocating unexplained necessity.

response.rationale: Oppy directly challenges the proposed asymmetry by asking what explanatory materials make divine necessity less brute than the natural starting point.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: The reply explicitly contacts the ultimate explanatory demand, although it precedes Pearce's fuller essence-based proposal.

precisionFindings.rationale: The symmetry challenge and its target—explanation of necessary divine existence—are clear and stable.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The interrogative form appropriately places an explanatory burden without claiming that no answer is possible.

charity.alternative: God's necessity might be grounded in divine essence rather than left as an unexplained starting point.
charity.decisiveQualification: At this stage the essence-based explanation has not yet been supplied, so the demand remains legitimate.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The symmetry objection follows clearly if both views terminate in an unexplained necessary starting point.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The challenge is conceptually well supported, though it does not yet compare the strongest essence-based theistic response.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It directly supports the central con bridge requiring symmetrical scrutiny of ultimate necessities.

representationalCharity.rationale: The move leaves room for the theist to provide distinctive explanatory materials and asks directly for them.

moves.evidenceBasis: Oppy asks how the necessity of a postulated God could be explained if the natural starting point is rejected as unexplained.

moves.speaker: Kenny Pearce
moves.proposition: Explanatory inquiry can legitimately terminate in autonomous facts that do not need explanation, with real and nominal definitions providing plausible examples.
moves.attributionBasis: Pearce immediately answers Oppy's challenge, adopts an explicit distinction, and develops it through definition-based examples to the context boundary.

components.text: What principled resource could terminate explanation for God without merely leaving divine necessity brute.

response.rationale: Pearce answers by distinguishing brute facts from autonomous facts and proposing real or nominal definitions as candidates that stand in no need of further explanation.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: The reply directly supplies the requested kind of terminus, though its success depends on a further account of definitional autonomy.

precisionFindings.rationale: The distinction between brute and autonomous facts is explicit, and definitions are presented as plausible candidates rather than guaranteed cases.

calibrationFindings.rationale: Pearce presents the definitional proposal as plausible and acknowledges that explanatory inquiry reaches some terminus.

charity.alternative: Definitions may describe essences without explaining why anything instantiating them exists.
charity.decisiveQualification: Pearce's proposal requires real definition to make the explanatory question mistaken, not merely linguistically settled.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The autonomous-fact distinction is coherent, but the inference from definitional status to no need of explanation remains material.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: A named philosophical distinction and examples support the proposal, while the decisive explanatory warrant is compressed.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It directly supports the pro route's central ultimate-terminus bridge by proposing a principled stopping condition.

representationalCharity.rationale: The response addresses the strongest symmetry concern but does not fully establish that real definitions carry existential force.

moves.evidenceBasis: Pearce distinguishes brute from autonomous facts and identifies real and nominal definitions as plausible explanatory termini.

moves.speaker: Kenny Pearce
moves.proposition: A maximally satisfying ultimate explanation would involve an entity whose real definition or essence entails actual existence, and God is a developed candidate for that role.
moves.attributionBasis: The uninterrupted turn continues Pearce's account of autonomous facts and ends immediately before Oppy's direct naturalistic objection.

response.rationale: This constructive move develops the preceding terminus proposal by identifying essence-entailing existence and God as a developed candidate.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within constructive moves, it provides the central positive terminus proposal while openly noting a naturalistic candidate.

precisionFindings.rationale: The ideal of maximal satisfaction and the description of God as a candidate are explicitly qualified rather than asserted categorically.

calibrationFindings.rationale: Pearce calls the proposal maximally satisfying and God a traditional candidate while conceding that naturalists can nominate alternatives.

charity.alternative: A naturalist could assign essence-entailing existence to fundamental particles or an initial state.
charity.decisiveQualification: Pearce acknowledges that option but reports finding it less plausible rather than declaring it incoherent.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The proposal is internally coherent, but the bridge from essence to actual existence is stated rather than demonstrated.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The move invokes a developed tradition and a conceptual ideal but supplies little argument for God's unique suitability.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It directly advances the indispensable pro bridge seeking a principled ultimate explanatory terminus.

representationalCharity.rationale: The strongest live naturalistic alternative is expressly recognized, though the basis for preferring God is underdeveloped.

moves.evidenceBasis: Pearce proposes entities whose real essence includes actual existence and presents God as a longstanding candidate while acknowledging naturalistic proposals.

moves.speaker: Graham Oppy
moves.proposition: A naturalist can nominate the universe's initial state as an entity whose essence includes existence, so that explanatory structure does not uniquely favor theism.
moves.attributionBasis: Oppy explicitly enters with a brief objection, and Pearce begins his answer in the following source row.

components.text: Whether essence-entailing existence supplies a comparative explanatory advantage unique to theism.
Whether the definitional stopping rule distinguishes a divine terminus from a natural initial state.

response.rationale: Oppy adopts Pearce's real-definition framework and nominates the universe's initial state as an equally available naturalistic candidate, directly defeating uniqueness rather than the framework itself.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: The reply explicitly contacts the comparative inference and gives a precise symmetric countercandidate within the proponent's own framework.

precisionFindings.rationale: The claim is narrowly framed as candidate availability and lack of a clear next comparative step.

calibrationFindings.rationale: Oppy claims only that a naturalist can nominate the initial state and that the subsequent advantage is unclear.

charity.alternative: God may possess a richer or better-developed essence than the universe's initial state.
charity.decisiveQualification: A richer description alone does not establish that essence entails existence more plausibly.

logicalCoherence.rationale: If the same essence-entailing status is available to a natural initial state, the claimed unique advantage does not follow.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The counterexample is tightly fitted to Pearce's concession, though its own metaphysical plausibility is not independently defended.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It directly supports the con central bridge denying an unsupported asymmetry between ultimate necessities.

representationalCharity.rationale: The objection accepts the theistic framework provisionally and isolates the unresolved comparative asymmetry.

moves.evidenceBasis: Oppy nominates the universe's initial state as a naturalistic entity whose essence includes existence and notes the resulting stalemate.

moves.speaker: Kenny Pearce
moves.proposition: Default trust in human cognitive faculties and testimony extends presumptively to the widespread practice of interpreting experiences as encounters with God or supernatural reality.
moves.attributionBasis: After the moderated topic transition, Pearce presents the religious-experience case continuously until Oppy asks what qualifies as such an experience.

response.rationale: This constructive move extends presumptive trust in cognition and testimony to widespread practices of interpreting experience religiously.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within constructive moves, it clearly states the epistemic principle and its religious application, though calibration is deferred.

precisionFindings.rationale: The default-trust thesis is clear, but the relevant class of faculties, practices, and religious interpretations remains broad.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The analogy with ordinary cognition supports a presumption, but extension to supernatural interpretation needs a more explicit defeater condition.

charity.alternative: Religious interpretation may be a culturally variable inference rather than a basic cognitive faculty.
charity.decisiveQualification: Default trust can extend to testimony and learned practices, but only with domain-specific calibration.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The extension from general cognitive trust to religious interpretation leaves a material bridge concerning relevant similarity.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: Widespread practice and general epistemic trust offer support, but unreliability, diversity, and alternative mechanisms are not compared.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It directly advances the central pro burden of assigning evidential weight to religious experience and testimony.

representationalCharity.rationale: The move does not caricature skepticism, yet it compresses the strongest distinction between experience and interpretation.

moves.evidenceBasis: Pearce identifies a widespread practice of interpreting experiences as encounters with supernatural reality and argues for default trust in it.

moves.speaker: Graham Oppy
moves.proposition: A broad category of religious experience is readily explained naturalistically, while a narrower evidentially stronger category raises doubts about how frequently such experiences occur.
moves.attributionBasis: Oppy poses a sustained definitional dilemma with personal and testimonial examples, ending when Pearce begins his analogy with arguments from evil.

components.text: Which experiences belong to the relevant religious category and how their prevalence relates to evidential strength.

response.rationale: Oppy directly presses a classificatory dilemma: broad categories are common but easily naturalized, while narrow stronger categories may be uncommon.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: The reply explicitly contacts both breadth and evidential force, though it asks for clarification rather than completing a naturalistic account.

precisionFindings.rationale: The broad-versus-narrow alternatives and their distinct evidential consequences are clearly specified.

calibrationFindings.rationale: Oppy frames the point as a demand for clarification and does not overclaim that either horn is conclusively established.

charity.alternative: A broad category can contain experiences of differing quality rather than having uniform evidential weight.
charity.decisiveQualification: The proponent must still specify how quality is assessed and how frequently strong cases occur.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The dilemma identifies a real tradeoff, but it is not exhaustive because breadth and quality can be separated.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The conceptual challenge is well motivated, though no frequency data or representative cases establish either empirical premise.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It directly supports the con central burden of calibrating religious experience against category breadth and reliability.

representationalCharity.rationale: The dilemma is fairly posed as a request for distinctions, though a quality-weighted broad category remains available.

moves.evidenceBasis: Oppy contrasts a common broad category readily naturalized with a narrower stronger category whose actual frequency is uncertain.

moves.speaker: Kenny Pearce
moves.proposition: Religious experience should be construed broadly and weighted by quality, while its first-person character can justify an experiencer's non-neutral stance despite disagreement.
moves.attributionBasis: Pearce directly answers Oppy's classificatory challenge through an extended analogy and epistemic account, ending before Oppy's next objection.

components.text: Whether a broad category of religious experience can retain evidential force without treating every instance equally.

response.rationale: Pearce accepts a broad category, differentiates experiences by quality, and adds that first-person access can justify a non-neutral stance for the experiencer.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: The reply directly contacts the breadth horn and supplies a quality-weighted alternative, though its calibration criteria remain compressed.

precisionFindings.rationale: The broad and first-person claims are recoverable, but experiential quality is not given a stable operational criterion.

calibrationFindings.rationale: Pearce makes a qualified epistemic claim for experiencers rather than claiming that all reports strongly justify outsiders.

charity.alternative: Broad mundane religious experiences may have low evidential value and be naturally explainable.
charity.decisiveQualification: Pearce expressly weights cases by quality and limits some justification to the first-person standpoint.

logicalCoherence.rationale: Quality weighting answers the false uniformity assumption, though the first-person privilege needs a fuller epistemic bridge.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The analogy and perspectival distinction are relevant, but no criteria verify quality or distinguish veridical from misleading cases.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It directly advances the pro central religious-experience bridge with calibrated, context-sensitive evidential weight.

representationalCharity.rationale: The reply preserves the force of Oppy's concern while denying that breadth requires uniform evidential treatment.

moves.evidenceBasis: Pearce construes religious experience broadly, distinguishes extraordinary from mundane cases, and emphasizes first-person justification.

moves.speaker: Graham Oppy
moves.proposition: Human faculties are not trusted without qualification; experience teaches the circumstances in which each faculty is unreliable.
moves.attributionBasis: The turn directly follows Pearce's account and is explicitly framed as a response to his claim about general trust.

components.text: Whether first-person trust in experience should be qualified by learned circumstances of faculty unreliability.
Whether human cognitive faculties are generally trusted without domain-specific calibration.

response.rationale: Oppy directly rejects unqualified general trust and replaces it with developmentally learned knowledge of when particular faculties are unreliable.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: The reply explicitly contacts the trust principle and states the relevant calibration requirement, though it remains general.

precisionFindings.rationale: The move consistently distinguishes ordinary reliance from learned, circumstance-sensitive limits on every faculty.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The general developmental claim is moderately framed and supported by familiar patterns of learned faculty limitation.

charity.alternative: Default trust may be defeasible rather than unconditional and thus compatible with later calibration.
charity.decisiveQualification: Pearce still needs a religious-domain account of when defeaters arise and how they alter evidential weight.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The distinction between baseline use and circumstance-sensitive reliability is coherent and directly relevant.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: Ordinary developmental experience supports the general point, but its specific application to religious cognition is not developed.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It directly supports the con central experience-calibration bridge by specifying learned conditions of unreliability.

representationalCharity.rationale: Oppy's wording risks treating default trust as unqualified, but the substantive calibration demand remains decisive.

moves.evidenceBasis: Oppy argues that people learn circumstances in which each faculty is unreliable rather than trusting faculties without qualification.

moves.speaker: Graham Oppy
moves.proposition: The disorder and ambiguity of religious experience fit nonintentional causes better than communication from an agent intending relationship with human beings.
moves.attributionBasis: Oppy develops an explicit disanalogy between inquiry into nonintentional objects and interaction with an intentional communicating agent.

components.text: Whether religious experiences fit intentional divine communication despite ambiguity and interpretive disorder.
Whether widespread religious interpretation warrants trust when the putative source is an intentional communicator.

response.rationale: Oppy distinguishes inquiry into nonintentional objects from communication by a relationship-seeking agent and argues that pervasive ambiguity is less expected in the latter case.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: The reply contacts the intentional-source implication and states a comparative expectation, though the target's primary focus was epistemic weight.

precisionFindings.rationale: The contrast between nonintentional objects and an intentional communicating agent is clear, with divine aims left implicit.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The move offers an expectation-based comparative claim rather than certainty, although assumptions about divine communicative aims remain implicit.

charity.alternative: A divine agent may value ambiguity, freedom, gradual interpretation, or goods other than uniform doctrinal transmission.
charity.decisiveQualification: Those aims require independent support if invoked to explain sustained communicative disorder.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The intentional-communication contrast is cogent, conditional on the assumed divine aim of recognizable relationship.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The analogy supports the expectation, but the move does not document the extent of disorder or compare developed divine-purpose models.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It directly advances the con central burden connecting religious ambiguity to expectations about intentional communication.

representationalCharity.rationale: The objection identifies a strong default expectation but does not fully incorporate the range of possible divine purposes.

moves.evidenceBasis: Oppy contrasts difficult inquiry into noncommunicating entities with the surprising disorder expected from an agent trying to communicate relationally.

moves.speaker: Kenny Pearce
moves.proposition: Religious experience need not primarily aim at uniform detailed theology and should instead be assessed through whole traditions, lived effects, testimony, and long-term communal functioning.
moves.attributionBasis: Pearce identifies the objection as a hiddenness puzzle, rejects a specific divine aim, and then gives his alternative method of evaluation.

components.text: Whether divine religious communication should be expected chiefly to produce uniform and detailed theological understanding.

response.rationale: Pearce identifies the objection as depending on a narrow divine aim, rejects that assumption, and proposes assessing traditions through lived effects, testimony, and long-term communal functioning.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: The reply directly challenges the expected aim and offers an alternative evaluative frame, but gives limited independent support for it.

precisionFindings.rationale: The rejected uniform-theology aim is clear, but the content and success conditions of the holistic divine purpose remain broad.

calibrationFindings.rationale: Pearce concedes that disorder can remain a problem for other views and proposes rather than proves a broader purpose.

charity.alternative: Even a holistic relational purpose may predict clearer and less conflicting divine communication.
charity.decisiveQualification: Rejecting uniform detailed theology reduces but does not eliminate the evidential force of enduring disorder.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The reorientation to holistic purposes is coherent, but the move needs a bridge showing why the observed diversity serves those purposes.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The alternative framework is plausible and qualified, yet its fit with actual traditions is asserted without representative comparison.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It directly advances the pro central diversity bridge by contesting uniform-theology expectations and proposing broader aims.

representationalCharity.rationale: Pearce expressly retains the objection as a problem for broader views instead of dismissing it entirely.

moves.evidenceBasis: Pearce denies that detailed uniform theology exhausts God's aims and recommends evaluating entire traditions, testimony, effects, and communal life.

moves.speaker: Graham Oppy
moves.proposition: The enduring diversity of radically different religious traditions resists a plausible single-religion account and is easier for naturalism to explain.
moves.attributionBasis: Oppy introduces the Rainbow Serpent tradition, compares it with several major religions, and explicitly draws the comparative naturalist conclusion.

components.text: Whether radically different enduring traditions admit a plausible unifying account under one divine purpose.

response.rationale: Oppy uses the sharp differences among isolated and major traditions to challenge a single unifying religious story and draws an explicit comparative advantage for naturalism.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: The reply directly contacts the holistic-unification demand and supplies a concrete diversity case, though the naturalistic mechanism is compressed.

precisionFindings.rationale: The claim is expressly comparative and presented as difficulty seeing a plausible unifying account, not as impossibility.

calibrationFindings.rationale: Oppy's conclusion that naturalism has an easier time is appropriately weaker than certainty and tracks the examples offered.

charity.alternative: Different traditions may contain genuine contact interpreted through culturally inherited conceptual frameworks.
charity.decisiveQualification: A unifying theistic account must explain both common contact and persistent radically divergent content.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The inference from radical diversity to comparative naturalistic fit is cogent, though not deductively decisive.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: Several contrasting traditions provide representative support, while the exact naturalistic causal account remains mostly implicit.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It directly supports the con central religious-disorder bridge through a comparative explanation of enduring diversity.

representationalCharity.rationale: The objection allows that a unifying story might be proposed but presses its comparative plausibility against substantial diversity.

moves.evidenceBasis: Oppy contrasts the Rainbow Serpent tradition with Christianity, Hinduism, and Buddhism and argues naturalism more easily accommodates their differences.

moves.speaker: Kenny Pearce
moves.proposition: A long-isolated religious tradition may reflect genuine experiences of God interpreted through its inherited framework rather than faculties wholly disconnected from reality.
moves.attributionBasis: Pearce acknowledges limited knowledge of the example, discusses the anthropological uncertainty, and formulates the competing theistic interpretation himself.

components.text: Whether an isolated and radically different tradition must count against genuine contact with one divine reality.

response.rationale: Pearce proposes that genuine experiences of God may be interpreted through inherited frameworks, thereby directly offering a unifying possibility for the isolated tradition.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: The reply contacts the decisive diversity example but remains tentative and does not fully explain the radically divergent content.

precisionFindings.rationale: The proposed interpretation is recoverable and carefully tentative, though genuine experience and inherited framework remain underspecified.

calibrationFindings.rationale: Pearce repeatedly signals limited knowledge and offers the theistic interpretation as a live possibility rather than a conclusion.

charity.alternative: The tradition's experiences may arise from ordinary human cognitive and cultural processes without contact with God.
charity.decisiveQualification: Mere compatibility with genuine divine contact does not show that this interpretation is comparatively better supported.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The interpretation is possible and coherent, but possibility alone does not answer the comparative explanatory challenge.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The speaker acknowledges limited knowledge and provides no independent evidence distinguishing divine contact from cultural construction.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It materially supports the pro central diversity bridge by applying the inherited-framework account to the decisive example.

representationalCharity.rationale: Pearce explicitly recognizes the naturalistic interpretation and asks whether the theist must adopt it, avoiding caricature.
